plan.title: The Embroidered Barrier

story.premise: In a sun-drenched haveli, two souls are separated by a heavy, ornate silk curtain that serves as both a physical and social barrier.
story.emotional_goal: To feel the presence of the other despite the impossibility of a direct encounter.
story.opening: Meera stands behind a semi-transparent embroidered curtain, watching the silhouette of Kabir on the other side.
story.turning_point: Kabir reaches out to touch the fabric, and Meera mirrors his gesture from the inside.
story.payoff: A gust of wind momentarily lifts the hem of the curtain, offering a fleeting, unblocked glimpse before the barrier settles back into place.

meera.description: A young woman in a teal and gold salwar kameez with a sheer dupatta.
meera.initial_state: Standing behind a heavy silk curtain in a shaded interior.

kabir.description: A young man in a simple white cotton kurta.
kabir.initial_state: Standing in a bright courtyard on the opposite side of the curtain.

curtain.description: A large, heavy silk curtain with intricate gold embroidery and floral patterns.
curtain.initial_state: Hanging still, completely dividing the space.

bible.style: Detailed painterly 2D illustration with a tactile paper finish, featuring soft watercolor textures and elegant linework.
bible.palette: Warm ochre, deep teal, dusty rose, and shimmering gold accents.
bible.characters: Meera has expressive eyes and traditional jewelry; Kabir has a contemplative expression and soft features.
bible.locations: A traditional Indian Haveli with carved sandstone arches, potted bougainvillea, and marble floors.
bible.motifs: Shadows on fabric, embroidery patterns, the play of light through sheer cloth.
bible.arc: A progression from distant observation to a moment of tactile connection, ending in a realization of the barrier's permanence.

scenes.label: The Approach
scenes.visual: A close-up of the curtain from the outside. Kabir's hand reaches into the frame and gently presses against the silk.
scenes.action: The fabric indents under the pressure of Kabir's fingers, stretching the gold embroidery.
scenes.meaning: He makes an effort to reach through the barrier.
scenes.after: The curtain shows the physical impression of a hand from the outside.

coverage.staging: Kabir stands close to the curtain, reaching out.
coverage.visible_event: The fabric deforms under Kabir's touch.
coverage.background_view: Warm sunlit courtyard outside the carved sandstone archway of a Rajasthani haveli, framing a heavy embroidered teal silk curtain hanging in the entrance.

story.purpose: Show the first physical interaction with the barrier from the other side.
story.link_from_previous: Kabir stops walking and engages with the curtain.
story.emotional_change: A sense of anticipation and tactile tension.

state_in.kabir: Stopping in front of the curtain outside.

state_out.meera: Sensing the pressure from the other side.
state_out.kabir: Pressing his hand against the curtain.

story_review.reason: The narrative provides a strong emotional progression that directly mirrors the song's lyrics about the 'parda' (curtain). It uses distinct camera setups—moving from the interior shadow to the exterior courtyard light, and from close-up tactile interactions to wide shots of parallel movement—to visualize the physical and social barrier. The 'Mirror Touch' provides a clear turning point, and the 'Fleeting Glimpse' at the end offers an earned, poetic payoff that fits the contemplative mood of the Ghazal without breaking the established logic of the barrier.
